def min_cross_flips(start, target):
    """Compute the minimum number of cross-flip operations needed to turn one
    binary grid into another, or decide that it is impossible.

    You are given two n-by-m binary grids, `start` and `target`, each encoded
    as a list of n strings of length m over the characters '0' and '1'
    (1 <= n <= 30, 1 <= m <= 30; both grids always have identical dimensions).

    One operation: choose any cell (i, j) of the grid. Every cell in row i is
    flipped (0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0), and every cell in column j is
    flipped. The chosen cell (i, j) itself lies in both the row and the
    column, so it is flipped twice and therefore ends up unchanged. In other
    words, a cell (r, c) changes value if and only if exactly one of
    r == i, c == j holds.

    Return the minimum number of operations required to transform `start`
    into `target`, as an int. If no sequence of operations (of any length,
    including repeats of the same cell) can achieve it, return -1. If the
    grids are already equal, return 0.

    Note that the state space has up to 2**900 configurations, so any search
    over grid states is hopeless; the answer must be derived from structural
    properties of the operation.

    Examples:

    >>> min_cross_flips(["00", "00", "00", "00"], ["01", "10", "10", "10"])
    1
    >>> min_cross_flips(["000"], ["111"])
    -1
    >>> min_cross_flips(["0000", "0000", "0000", "0000"], ["0011", "0011", "0011", "0011"])
    2
    """
